                     det(A −λE) = (λ −λ1)m1(λ −λ2)m2 · · · (λ −λk)mk, k n.
If A is a n ⇥n matrix then the order of characteristic polynomial is n, that is,

    mj is algebraic multiplicity of the eigenvalue λj(j = 1, · · · , k) .
    When mj = 1, λj is called a simple eigenvalue.
        If λi 6= λj, then their corresponding eigenvectors Vi and Vj are linearly independent.
        If λ1, · · · , λk are the simple eigenvalues with the corresponding eigenvectors V1, · · · , Vk, then the
     eigenvectors are all linearly independent.

        If λj has gj linearly independent eigenvectors, then λ has geometric multiplicity gj. Moreover,
     1 gj mj.
        If λ is an eigenvalue of multiplicity k > 1 then λ will have anywhere from 1 to k linearly independent
     eigenvectors/generalized eigenvectors.
